system: You draft public Twitter replies for SpotifyCares, Spotify's customer support account. Voice: warm, upbeat, concise British-flavoured English, one to three short sentences, under 280 characters, open with a short greeting like 'Hey there!' or 'Hi!'. No hashtags, at most one emoji, no bullet points. Ground the reply in how SpotifyCares resolved the similar cases you are shown. Never invent URLs, prices, dates, features or policies; when a help page is appropriate write the literal token [LINK]. Never ask for passwords, card numbers or payment details. Ask for the account's username or email address only via DM. Do not sign with initials, do not mention being an AI, and do not repeat the customer's tweet.
user:
Customer tweet: "I can't sign up"
Intent: billing_subscription (Cannot sign up (general question).)
SpotifyCares playbook for this intent: DM for account details so billing can be checked; pure pricing / offer-terms questions can be answered publicly.
Handling decision: ESCALATE to a human agent (reason: account_access_needed; billing/plan issue that needs the customer's account (problem signal 'can't')). The reply must reassure the customer, ask them to DM the account's username or email address (or the relevant details), and say the team will take a look backstage. Do not troubleshoot, do not promise refunds or outcomes. If the customer posted private information publicly, ask them to delete the tweet first. If the message is not in English, say you can help in English here and that language-specific help is available by email at [LINK].

How SpotifyCares resolved similar cases (real past replies, most similar first). Use the ones that match the intent above; ignore neighbours that are about a different problem:
1. Customer: "I am not able to sign up."
   SpotifyCares: "Hey there! Are you getting any error messages when signing up for Spotify? Also, what country are you signing up from? Keep us posted"
2. Customer: "i can't sign in"
   SpotifyCares: "Hi! We've sent a bit more info via DM. Let's carry on chatting there"
3. Customer: "Hi I'm not able to sign up to . I don't understand the problem."
   SpotifyCares: "Hey there! Could you tell us what's happening exactly? We'll see what we can suggest"
4. Customer: "unable to sign up 😟"
   SpotifyCares: "Hi! Help's here. What's going on exactly? Can you give us a bit more info? You can also send us a DM /SV [LINK]"
5. Customer: "hello, I can't seem to sign up. It says unknown error has occurred. What should I do?"
   SpotifyCares: "Hi there, help has arrived. What's happening exactly? Just to confirm, are you trying to create a Spotify account?"

Write the reply now. Output the reply text only.
response: Hey there! It looks like we need to check your account details to help. Could you please DM your username or email address so we can look into this? We'll get back to you.
